generatedProse.concept-context: In psychology, a working creative practice helps most on open tasks, such as framing your own research question or designing a study. You treat the task as a chance to practise, generate rough ideas before judging, then choose the strongest and refine it. Run that way across a module, each part starts to feel natural.
generatedProse.worked-example: Two psychology students get the same open brief: design a small study on the module theme. Tom waits for one strong idea, judges it at once, and decides he is not creative. Amara treats it as a practice: she lists rough designs, keeps the best alive, then chooses and refines one. Over the term, Amara's proposals grow stronger, because creativity became a habit rather than a one-off.
generatedProse.summary: In psychology, creativity is most useful as a working practice. You treat it as a skill, move between generating and choosing, and keep the barriers loose, across each task. It is the habit, not any single idea, that strengthens how you study.

check.body: A student faces an open essay question. They treat it as a chance to practise, list several rough ideas without judging, then choose and refine the strongest. What does this show?

items.text: Their next round of learning and preparation, which is why the following report improved.
Nothing; feedback comes at the end, so it cannot affect anything that follows.
Only the mark on the first report, which cannot now change.
The deadline for the next report.

feedback.correct: That's right. Using the feedback fed back into the next round of learning and preparation, which is why the following report improved: that is the cycle working.
feedback.incorrectNotFinal: Not quite. Think about what the student changed before the next report, not the old mark or the deadline.
feedback.incorrectFinal: Using the feedback fed back into the student's next round of learning and preparation, which is why the next report improved. The old mark cannot change and the deadline is not part of the cycle; feedback is not the end, it feeds the next turn.

_items.text: That creativity is working as one practice: the skill, the two modes and loosening the barriers all turn up on the same task.
_items.feedback: Yes. All three ideas are at work together, which is what the practice looks like.

_items.text: That the student is naturally gifted and did not need to practise.
_items.feedback: The student practised on purpose. That is the skill at work, not a gift.

_items.text: That generating ideas is the only part of creativity that matters.
_items.feedback: Generating is one part. The student also chose and refined, which is convergent thinking.

_items.text: That judging ideas early is the best way to start an essay.
_items.feedback: The student held judging back at first. That is what let the rough ideas appear.
